<!-- docs-drift-check -->
### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **1** package(s): `@objectstack/rest`, touching **22** documentable anchor(s).

**19** hand-written doc(s) name something this change touched — list omitted above 15 rows. Re-derive on the tree named below: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 2e1562091cf850d7f3d1057f5ebb82e9ff8cb0be`.

⛔ **5** release-owned page(s) also affected — read-only, see AGENTS.md Documentation Guardrails.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **4** cross-cutting symbol(s) contributed no route anchor: `enforceAuth (23 routes)`, `resolveExecCtx (28 routes)`, `routeManager (19 routes)`, `resolveProtocol (25 routes)`
- the SDK route bridge reached **54** of **206** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **152** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **152**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **97** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **18** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 2e1562091cf850d7f3d1057f5ebb82e9ff8cb0be` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `be80cf625e5a1a8006275e1ea7200925b00f481a` — the merge of head `5da02e4b97d67a88a6a47f766613e51c1a12bc61` into base `2e1562091cf850d7f3d1057f5ebb82e9ff8cb0be`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin be80cf625e5a1a8006275e1ea7200925b00f481a && git checkout be80cf625e5a1a8006275e1ea7200925b00f481a
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 2e1562091cf850d7f3d1057f5ebb82e9ff8cb0be 5da02e4b97d67a88a6a47f766613e51c1a12bc61 && git checkout -B drift-repro 2e1562091cf850d7f3d1057f5ebb82e9ff8cb0be && git merge --no-ff 5da02e4b97d67a88a6a47f766613e51c1a12bc61

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 2e1562091cf850d7f3d1057f5ebb82e9ff8cb0be
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 2e1562091cf850d7f3d1057f5ebb82e9ff8cb0be` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `TIER_DEFAULT`
Head-sha: `5da02e4b97d67a88a6a47f766613e51c1a12bc61`
Local-runs: none

**Face:** the declaration face. This is a move-only slice of `@objectstack/rest`, and no token of the moved body changed. The diff does five things:
- it moves one registrar body into one new module, `packages/rest/src/ui-routes.ts`;
- it moves one module-level type alias, `TransportScopedMetaRequest`, into that module with the body, and `rest-server.ts` imports it back;
- it grows the registrar list 10 → 11 and re-points the nine readers of that list;
- it re-points one gate's target table, `scripts/check-route-envelope.mjs`;
- it adds the stub, one import, two pointer comments and their notes to `rest-server.ts`.

The 13-file list holds no published schema and no governed path. `record-recognisers --template --paths` over that list derives `TIER_DEFAULT`. `Governed Surface Queue Guard` concluded success. The PR body reads `Clause-②: no` with no arm, and the diff adds no changeset.

**Inputs:**
- card #23050: its body and all 42 comments. These include the triage `6126748916`, slice 1's acceptance `6135541164` and landing `6136102437`, slice 2's refinement `6189011700`, the seat ruling on the `static` receiver `6205442867`, the seat ruling on providers in `6215084478`, the slice 10 claim `6218443248` and the slice 10 `os-dev-report` `6220278484`;
- slice 9's record `6217704682` on PR #23959, used as precedent;
- PR #23990:
  - its body;
  - its file list: 13 files, +347 / −130, which matches `git diff --numstat` file for file;
  - its one comment, the advisory Docs Drift Check;
  - its timeline: the labels, and the declaration `6220378958` on #6017;
- the net diff against the merge base `0b6956490a`;
- the 44 check-runs on this head, read last.

**Method:** read-only. Every count below was read off the git objects of the merge base and the head with `git show`, text `diff` and `grep`, plus one text-only count script. That script applies each reader's own rule to the text: the execctx site, mention and forwarder rules; the ui-view pair's three spellings; the dogfood population rule with its forwarder slice and controls; the docblock opener and stacking rule; `querySlots`; the draft and coercion tokens; the two realtime tripwire regexes. No repository code was built, tested or re-run.

The merge base's `rest-server.ts` blob (`1c7f7e45a9`) is the same blob as at the dev's base `68ffa5dc1a`. Between those two commits nothing changed under `packages/rest`, in the gate, in `packages/spec/liveness` or in `scripts/adr-anchors`. Only two checklist areas and one new dogfood test changed, and that test reads no `rest-server.ts`. So the PR's base line numbers apply as written. The merge commit `5da02e4b97` changes none of the 13 files.

### ① Derived judgments

No accept set changes and no public surface changes. Each change the diff makes is judged below.

1. **The moved body is byte-identical once de-indented: right.**
   - Base `rest-server.ts` `:8314`–`:8373` is 60 lines. With one 4-space indent removed, it equals head `ui-routes.ts` `:118`–`:177`. `diff` finds 0 differing lines.
   - Every non-empty line in the range starts with 4 spaces. The range has one empty line and no trailing whitespace.
   - Its two template literals, `${basePath}/ui` (base `:8314`) and `${uiPath}/view/:object/:type` (`:8320`), each sit on one line. Every other backtick in the range is in a line comment. So removing the indent changed no runtime string.
   - The body has no `RestServer.` access. The `static` exception was not used, and no token changed.
   - The rest of `rest-server.ts` changes in four hunks, +21 / −101 in total:
     - the `GetUiViewRequest` import name removed, with a 2-line pointer (head `:151`–`:152`);
     - the alias block removed (40 lines), with a 4-line pointer (head `:261`–`:264`);
     - the new import and its comment (head `:311`–`:312`);
     - the stub: 13 lines in place of the 60-line body (head `:8280`–`:8294`).
   - The removed lines add up: 1 + 40 + 60 = 101. The file goes from 9,995 to 9,915 lines.
   - The private method keeps its name, its JSDoc and its position. Base `:8284`–`:8313` and head `:8251`–`:8280` diff to 0.
   - `registerRoutes` is identical: base `:4790`–`:4864` against head `:4757`–`:4831`, 75 lines, `diff` empty.
     - The call site moved from base `:4805` to head `:4772` only because of the lines removed above it.
     - It is still guarded by `api.enableUi` and still sits between `registerMetadataEndpoints` and `registerSearchEndpoints`. So the registration order holds on every base.

2. **The host lists exactly what the body reads: right.**
   - The body's code reads of `this.` (comments excluded), one each:
     - `routeManager` (module `:122`);
     - `resolveRequestEnvironmentId` (`:133`);
     - `resolveExecCtx` (`:146`);
     - `enforceAuth` (`:147`);
     - `enforceEnvironmentOwnership` (`:148`);
     - `resolveProtocol` (`:149`).
   - No comment in the body mentions `this.`.
   - `UiRouteHost` (`:102`–`:109`) declares exactly these 6, in that order. Each is typed by indexed access on the class.
   - The body has no bare `this`, no element access on `this` and no `function` keyword.
   - Its module-level free identifiers are exactly three:
     - `handleRouteError`, imported from `./error-response.js`, the module `rest-server.ts` imports it from. `rest-server.ts` still uses it (31 → 30 mentions), so its own import stays.
     - `GetUiViewRequest`, imported as a type from `@objectstack/spec/api`. At base `rest-server.ts` had 2 mentions: the import and this use. So moving the import name is right.
     - `TransportScopedMetaRequest`, the moved alias (item 4).
   - The module's only import from `./rest-server.js` is `import type { RestServer }`. It is erased at build, so this slice adds no runtime import cycle.
   - So the seat's count of six members, one read each, holds.

3. **Value or closure, member by member: right.**
   - **`routeManager` goes by value.**
     - Its one read is the top-level `register` call, which runs during registration.
     - The class assigns the field only in the constructor (head `:2138`) and in the try/finally swap around `registerMetadataEndpointsInner` (`:5146` / `:5150`, inside `registerMetadataEndpoints`).
     - The UI registrar has one call site (`:4772`), and it runs after `registerMetadataEndpoints` has returned. So it is outside that window.
     - The interface marks the member `readonly`.
   - **The five methods go as late-bound closures.** Their receiver is still the server, so a spy set on the server after registration is still the one reached.
   - **No getter is owed.** The body reads no field at request time. The environment, the caller, the ownership verdict and the protocol are each resolved per request by a method.
   - **No provider is read,** so the seat's provider ruling (`6215084478`) does not apply.
   - The dev's late-binding measurement, its closure ablation and its base leg are the dev's, not re-run here. They match this reading, including the ruled guard order.

4. **`TransportScopedMetaRequest` moved verbatim, is still one declaration, and reaches nothing published: right.**
   - **Verbatim.** Base `rest-server.ts` `:260`–`:299` (the docblock and the declaration, 40 lines) against head `ui-routes.ts` `:54`–`:93`. The only differing line is the last one, which gains `export `.
   - **One declaration.** At head the tree holds one declaration of the name, `ui-routes.ts` `:93`, and `rest-server.ts` holds none. `rest-server.ts` imports it type-only at `:312`.
     - Its typed uses there go from 14 to 12 lines: the declaration and the UI use left, and the 12 other uses stay.
     - This is exactly slice 1's shape for `ServerScopedDataRequest` (declared in `data-action-routes.ts` `:157`, imported back at `rest-server.ts` `:278`).
   - **Nothing reaches the published `.d.ts`:**
     - `@objectstack/rest` publishes `dist`, `README.md` and `CHANGELOG.md` only.
     - Its build runs the root `tsup.config.ts`: one entry, `src/index.ts`, with `splitting: false`.
     - `src/index.ts` is untouched. It has no `export *`. It re-exports from `./rest-server.js` by name only: `RestServer`, the types `RestProtocol` and `MountedRoute`, and `metaItemPackageBinding`. It names no `ui-routes` module.
     - **No public `RestServer` signature names the alias.** All 12 uses are local `const` annotations inside private members: `metaListSource`, `serveMetaItemLayered`, `registerMetadataEndpointsInner` (7), `readFormObjectDefinitions` and `registerFormEndpoints` (2). A private member is emitted in the `.d.ts` with no type at all.
     - `UiRouteHost` and `registerUiEndpoints` appear only inside a private method body, which declaration emit does not reach.
   - The dev's `.d.ts` sha `7489de84…` and the two export-in-place counterfactuals (`a82fe845…`) are the dev's evidence, not re-run here. They are what this construction predicts, and slice 1 measured the same thing.

5. **No other module-level helper gained an export: right.**
   - The diff adds or removes no `export` line in `rest-server.ts`. It has 39 lines starting with `export ` at base and at head.
   - `ui-routes.ts` exports three names: the alias, `UiRouteHost` and `registerUiEndpoints`. None is reachable from `src/index.ts`.

6. **The registrar list and every reader were re-counted, and no reader was loosened: right.**
   - The list grows 10 → 11 by one appended entry. Exactly nine files import it, at base and at head, and all nine are in the diff. Each moves its length pin 10 → 11.
   - **execctx census.** Its site rule counts lines that hold `this.resolveExecCtx(environmentId, req)`.
     - Sites: 62 at both. Base 23 + 9 + 5 + 7 + 8 + 1 + 5 + 2 + 1 + 1; head 22 + 9 + 5 + 7 + 8 + 1 + 5 + 2 + 1 + 1 + 1.
     - Split: 46 bare / 16 caught at both. The UI site is bare, and the `enforceAuth` guard is its next line (`:147`).
     - Mentions of `resolveExecCtx`: 121 → 125. `rest-server.ts` goes 59 → 60 (one site out, one forwarder's 2 mentions in). The module holds 3 (the site 1, the interface member 2).
     - Forwarder lines in `rest-server.ts`: 11 → 12. The pin is exact: (11 − 1) + 3 − 1 = 12.
     - Neither map gains an entry. That is right: the module carries one registrar, and that registrar reads the seam.
   - **ui-view pair** (counted over the list):
     - `this.enforceAuth(` 58 → 59 and `this.resolveExecCtx(` 73 → 74. `rest-server.ts` stays at 19 and 34 (one site out, one forwarder in). The floors of 40 are unchanged.
     - **The ownership pin split is exact, not a loosening.**
       - The old pin was spellings of `this.enforceEnvironmentOwnership(` over the list, exactly 1. The method's declaration never matched that spelling, so the 1 was the call site.
       - Over the eleven files the spelling now reads 2: the call site (moved to `ui-routes.ts` `:148`) and the host literal's forwarder (`rest-server.ts` `:8290`). The forwarder string contains the spelling once, so the subtraction counts each forwarder exactly once.
       - The new pins are forwarders exactly 1 and non-forwarder spellings exactly 1. Together they admit one state only, as the old pin did.
       - A second call site reds (2). A second forwarder reds (2). A forwarder respelt, for example as a bound method, reds (0). A call site written in the forwarder's shape counts as a forwarder and reds (2).
       - Its reach is the same list as before. So the call-site count still holds at 1, and no state the old pin refused is now accepted.
     - **The sliced readings were re-pointed correctly.**
       - Both tests now slice `ui-routes.ts` from `export function registerUiEndpoints(` to the first column-0 closing brace after it. That brace is the function's own (`:178`, the file's last line), so the slice is exactly the function.
       - Each sliced term occurs once in the slice, in the asserted order: `resolveRequestEnvironmentId`, `resolveExecCtx`, `enforceAuth`, `enforceEnvironmentOwnership`, `resolveProtocol`.
       - Every assertion on the slice is positive, and the new slice is narrower than the old one (which ran on to `private registerCrudEndpoints(` and took in that method's JSDoc). So no assertion got weaker.
       - The dev's reason is right: the host literal spells the four guarded terms in the same order while calling none of them in a route. A slice of `rest-server.ts` would now pass the order assertions vacuously.
       - That the private method still mounts the one route stays pinned at runtime: the identity test's §6 wraps each private registrar on the prototype and asserts `registerUiEndpoints` mounts exactly the UI route.
   - **dogfood blind-spot row:**
     - `this.routeManager.register(` stays at 63 = 20 + 9 + 5 + 7 + 8 + 1 + 6 + 4 + 1 + 1 + 1.
     - `private register*Endpoints(` 16, `registerPerItemRoute(` 8, `const registerPerItemRoute =` 1 and the forwarder slice 1 are each unchanged.
     - The population 70 / 19 / 51 is unchanged. The UI door is outside `registerMetadataEndpoints` before and after.
     - **`enforceAuth` goes 104 → 108**: `rest-server.ts` 43 → 44, and the module 3.
       - The four new mentions are the seam once: the forwarder 2, the interface member 2.
       - The one call site moved and is counted in both readings. No call site was added.
       - It is an exact re-anchor, as in slices 3–9.
     - The new control `ui-routes.ts: this.routeManager.register(` reads 1. `registrar list length` reads 11.
     - `populationRule` now names the new module and the moved registrar.
   - **docblock pin:**
     - The module has exactly 4 TSDoc openers (`:3`, `:54`, `:95`, `:111`), none stacked, and its floor is 4.
     - The `//` note above the moved alias block sits above its opener, so the block still binds the declaration at `:93`.
     - `rest-server.ts` gives up only the alias's block: 164 → 163 (floor 100). Nothing there became stacked.
     - The floors' sum goes 40 → 44 = 4 + 3 + 3 + 8 + 3 + 8 + 5 + 3 + 3 + 4, and the sum is pinned exactly.
   - **query-number 9, canonical-query 4, meta-draft 8:**
     - The module has 0 `Number` / `parseInt` / `parseFloat` tokens and no unary plus. The body reads its two path parameters as strings.
     - It has 0 `query:` slot lines (by `querySlots`' own regex) and 0 draft tokens.
     - Each new floor is 0, and each sum is unchanged.
   - **dogfood realtime tripwires:** both probe regexes read 0 on each of the eleven files.

7. **`scripts/check-route-envelope.mjs` is re-pointed, not loosened: right.**
   - The gate's diff is +31 / −2. The two removed lines are the `rest-server.ts` row's two numbers, 16 and 14, now 15 and 13, each with a "NOT progress — the same MOVE" history comment. The rest is one new `MODULES` entry and its comment. No rule or other entry changes.
   - Counted on the module by `scanSource`'s own rules, over its two `.json(` calls:
     - `:165`, `res.json(view)`: the argument is not an object literal, so it counts toward neither dialect;
     - `:167`, the 501 body with a string-literal `error` and a top-level `code: 'NOT_IMPLEMENTED'`: `stringError` 1 and `siblingCode` 1.
     - So both counts are 1, as declared.
   - `rest-server.ts` loses exactly those two `.json(` lines, and the stub has none. So its row drops by exactly 1 and 1.
   - Both sums hold, read off the head's table:
     - `stringError`: 15 + 13 + 8 + 1 + 0 + 0 + 0 + 0 + 1 + 0 + 1 = 39;
     - `siblingCode`: 13 + 15 + 8 + 9 + 4 + 1 + 0 + 0 + 3 + 0 + 1 = 54.
   - `auditDialectOnly` requires each count to equal its pin and reds in both directions. So the pins are as tight as before.
   - The new entry is `dialectOnly` with ratchet `#9559`, like the nine moved modules before it.
   - The module matches `discover()`'s `*-routes.ts` convention, so an undeclared one reds `NOT DECLARED` (the dev's red-before reading). A `MODULES` declaration also takes the file out of the express-writer walk (`discoverExpressRoutes`), so no `EXPRESS_RESPONSE_MODULES` entry is owed.
   - `Lint · docs & code guards` and `Lint & Repo Gates` concluded success.

8. **The readers left untouched read no moved line: right.**
   - **Line citations:** the tree holds 51 `rest-server.ts:NNNN` citations outside released CHANGELOG text. None falls in a moved range (base `:260`–`:299`, `:8284`–`:8374`).
   - **ADR anchors:** neither moved range cites an `ADR-NNNN`, so no anchor is owed. `packages__rest__src__rest-server.ts.json` names no moved token. No ADR names `registerUiEndpoints` or the alias; every ADR hit on the search terms is a `ui/view.zod.ts` path.
   - **`packages/spec`:**
     - `liveness/rest_api.json` `:49` cites `rest-server.ts#registerRoutes` for the `if (this.config.api.enableUi)` gate. That line did not move (head `:4771`).
     - No liveness evidence string quotes a moved line. The probe strings `uiPath`, `UI View resolution`, `isScoped = basePath.includes` and `routeEnvironmentId` each read 0 there.
     - `protocol.zod.ts` (5) and `protocol.test.ts` (7) name the alias as `packages/rest`'s, never by file. So they stay true.
   - **The platform checklist:** the only item that names both `rest-server.ts` and a search term is `access-security.json` item 14. Its hit is the path `src/ui/views`, and its anchor is `#registerFormEndpoints`. No checklist anchor names the UI registrar or the alias.
   - **Every other mention of `registerUiEndpoints`** is one of the 13 diff files, or prose that names the method without a file: `authz-conformance.matrix.ts` `:20`, `authz-conformance.test.ts` `:181` / `:201`, the dogfood census notes, `rest-route-ledger.ts` `:129` and `packages/runtime/src/route-ledger.ts` `:181`. The private method still exists and still mounts the route, so each stays true.
   - **Other source readers of `rest-server.ts`** read tokens the move does not carry. `objectql-slot-consumer-census` counts `objectQLProvider`: 14 in `rest-server.ts` at both, 0 in the moved body. The test that names the UI route and the ownership guard (`rest-exec-ctx-principal-kind.test.ts` `:308`) does so in a comment and drives the route at runtime.
   - **Gates that walk `packages/rest/src`** still reach the moved code in its new file.
   - **Pre-existing stale prose, moved verbatim:** two items, none of them read by a gate (③ items 2 and 3).

### ② Semver level

- **`skip-changeset` is right.** Nothing a released package publishes changes.
  - **`@objectstack/rest`:**
    - The `.d.ts` and the export list hold by construction (① items 4 and 5).
    - The routes and their registration order hold by the move (① item 1).
    - The bundle's code is reorganised (the moved function and its `.call`), with no change to any behaviour, export, type or route. So there is nothing for a changelog to say.
  - **The rest of the diff:**
    - tests, including `@objectstack/dogfood`'s (a `private` package);
    - the test-side registrar list, which `src/index.ts` does not reach;
    - comments;
    - one gate's target table.
  - **The one runtime difference is the handler's `this`.** It is now the host literal, not the server. The body reaches the server only through the six handed members, and each method forwards to the server. A stack trace gains one forwarder frame, which the execctx census skips by design. No shipped wiring can observe it.
  - A move that changes no behaviour is not a feature or a fix. So no `patch` changeset is owed. Slices 1–9 landed on the same reading.
- **`Clause-②: no` is right.**
  - The door reads `req.params.object`, `req.params.type` and, on the scoped mount, `req.params.environmentId`, as before. What it passes to `getUiView` is unchanged.
  - No route is added or removed, and no `spec` key moves.
  - No accept set widens or narrows, so no `(narrowing)` arm is owed.
  - Line 2 of the PR body carries the line. No changeset exists to carry it a second time.
- **The changeset check's history:**
  - `Check Changeset` concluded failure at 16:43:59Z, before the label.
  - `skip-changeset` was written at 16:49:46Z by `objectstack-fleet[bot]`, the seat's write path.
  - The re-run concluded `skipped` at 16:49:49Z.

### ③ Boundary flags

Every dev flag is answered or escalated. The flags come from the PR body's Acceptance notes and from the report's (`6220278484`) `deviations`, `out_of_scope_findings` and `open_questions`.

1. **open_questions[0]: where `TransportScopedMetaRequest` finally lives. ESCALATED to the seat, non-blocking.**
   - Today's home is correct: one declaration, no copy, nothing published moved (① item 4). It is unexpected, because the alias serves the `/meta` doors and the form doors, not the UI door.
   - This record's reading agrees with the dev's recommendation **A**: the `/meta` slice moves it beside its users, or into one small shared module (which `ServerScopedDataRequest` could share). That is slice 1's ruling A for `ServerScopedDataRequest`.
   - **For the seat:** rule it, and name the carry in the `/meta` slice's claim. Its 12 uses sit in 5 members: `registerMetadataEndpointsInner` holds 7, the meta helpers `metaListSource` and `serveMetaItemLayered` hold 2, and `registerFormEndpoints` and `readFormObjectDefinitions` hold 3. So the forms slice is a reader of it too.
